exposure: Social Security Institute for Civil Servants
cohort: 600,124 first-time mothers giving birth after at least 37 weeks of gestation in Mexico in 2014
finding: The prevalence of primary cesarean delivery among first-time mothers in Mexico was very high (48.7%) and varied significantly by insurance coverage type and birthing facility, with Seguro Popular enrollees having a lower risk even after adjusting for covariates.
mod_finding: The study found a high prevalence of cesarean deliveries (48.7%) among first-time mothers in Mexico, with significant variations across insurance coverage types.
